# Potluck

> Potluck is free, open-source software (Apache-2.0) that puts a team's idle Macs and Linux machines to work: self-hosted GitHub Actions runners and sandboxes for coding agents, each job in a fresh VM or sandbox that is thrown away afterwards. It is made by Sengi.

Potluck is a program (`potluck`) for macOS and Linux. One machine runs a pool; friends and teammates join with a one-time code and lend machines to it. Work goes to a machine that is free, and a machine's owner can take it back at any time. There are no accounts: machines find each other over Tailscale (or a tunnel you set up).

- Install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sengirunners/potluck/main/install.sh | sh`
- Source, issues and documentation: https://github.com/sengirunners/potluck
- Releases: https://github.com/sengirunners/potluck/releases
- Maker: Sengi, https://sengi.run

## Pages

- [Potluck: self-hosted GitHub Actions runners and AI agent sandboxes on your team's idle machines](https://potluck.sh/): Potluck puts your team's idle Macs and Linux boxes to work: self-hosted GitHub Actions runners and sandboxes for coding agents, each job in a fresh VM or sandbox. Free and open source (Apache-2.0), early.
- [Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner with a fresh VM for every job](https://potluck.sh/github-actions-runner): Run GitHub Actions jobs on your team's idle Macs and Linux boxes, each job in a fresh VM or sandbox thrown away after it. Runs from forks are refused unless you allow them on a private repository. Free and open source.
- [Tart VMs for CI and agents: what Tart does, its licence, and what Potluck adds](https://potluck.sh/tart): Tart runs macOS and Linux VMs on Apple silicon. What it does, its FSL-1.1-ALv2 licence, Apple's two-VM limit, and what Potluck adds to use it for GitHub Actions jobs and coding agents.

## Blog

- [How to pool your team's spare Macs and Linux boxes for builds and coding agents](https://potluck.sh/blog/pool-spare-macs-and-linux-boxes-for-builds-and-agents.md): How a pool of a team's or friends' spare computers works: who can use whose machine, what a machine owner shares, and how a Mac owner takes it back.
- [How to run Claude Code and Codex in a sandbox on your own machines instead of a hosted sandbox service](https://potluck.sh/blog/run-coding-agents-in-a-sandbox-on-your-own-machines.md): Give Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent a throwaway sandbox on a Mac or Linux box you own. What a sandbox must isolate, and how Potluck sets it up.
- [How to run a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner on your own Mac, with a fresh VM for each job](https://potluck.sh/blog/self-hosted-github-actions-runner-on-your-mac.md): Run GitHub Actions jobs on your own Mac or Mac mini, each in a fresh throwaway VM, so one job never touches your files or the next job.
